Fields: (reapply) knobs only take effect once Reapply Cloth (or a redeploy) rebuilds the bepu sim with these values.
Bepu's Coulomb friction coefficient (0 = frictionless, unbounded above).

Canopy node collision sphere radius, as a FRACTION OF CANOPY DIAMETER. Must stay under pi*ReefRatio/(2*Spokes) (~0.039 at ReefRatio 0.4) or the reefed hem's own nodes overlap and hold the canopy open. Baked into the bepu sim at build time - only takes effect on Reapply Cloth / redeploy, not live.
Collision sphere size for clustered neighbor canopies as a fraction of their radius. Under 1 lets hems press together and merge; 1 keeps whole canopies apart and churns contacts.
Damping on the attractor spring. Default keeps the critically-damped 2*sqrt(gain) ratio but is tunable independently.
Draws the terrain patch the cloth actually collides against, in green. If it doesn't sit on the visible ground, the Ccf -> chute-local snapshot is off.

Exact-exponential relaxation of node velocity toward the local air velocity. The primary physical damping - cloth in air is overwhelmingly air-damped. Ramps to this full rate by Reference Q For Drag and stays there above it; 0 at vacuum, independent of Aero Gain.
Floor on pressure accel so a fully-filled canopy stays inflated even at low descent q.
Floor on the canopy attractor scale at low Fill, so the lattice never collapses to a point.
Lets canopy nodes collide with each other, stopping the cloth folding through itself. Costs extra broadphase pairs.
Multiplies (line length + diameter) for the max distance any node may sit from the pin. Guards against runaway line stretch.
Scales canopy internal pressure accel with dynamic pressure (QLocal / ReferenceQ).
Scales the aerodynamic drag accel applied to canopy-facing nodes.
Sideways nudge on a grounded deflating canopy so it drapes beside the vessel instead of on top. 0 disables.
Solver velocity iterations per substep; rounds down to an int at sim build time. Baked into the bepu sim at build time - only takes effect on Reapply Cloth / redeploy, not live.

Spring damping ratio shared by the structural/shear/bend constraints. 1 = critically damped; raise this if a settled canopy hums instead of sleeping. Heavy damping (default 40) is intentional for canopy cloth - values below ~10 read as jelly.
Spring frequency for bend (skip-neighbor) constraints. Controls canopy stiffness against folding.
Spring frequency for diagonal shear constraints. Controls how much the canopy resists skewing.
Spring frequency for structural (direct neighbor) constraints. Higher = stiffer, less stretch.
Spring gain pulling cloth nodes toward the analytic (attractor) inflated pose.

Suspension line / riser node collision radius, as a FRACTION OF CANOPY DIAMETER. Kept well below the canopy's because the line chains converge on the confluence - too large and they shove each other apart, bowing the lines outward when reefed. Baked into the bepu sim at build time - only takes effect on Reapply Cloth / redeploy, not live.
The QLocal at which Air Drag Rate reaches full strength (linear ramp from 0 at vacuum). Lower this to restore low-q damping without touching high-q behavior.
Trust-region cap on a single substep's displacement, as a fraction of canopy diameter. Guards against a single dynamic substep flinging a node.
Velocity decay rate, applied as exp(-rate*dt): substep-size invariant, unlike a per-substep constant factor. Keep low - it's a numerical-hygiene floor, not the primary damping (see Air Drag Rate).
Literals: (reapply) knobs only take effect once Reapply Cloth (or a redeploy) rebuilds the bepu sim with these values.

The atmospheric pressure at which the exhaust from this engine will be optimally expanded. This should be close to the pressure at the altitude where this engine will operate.
The diameter of the nozzle throat. This is the end of the converging section of the nozzle where gas velocity reaches Mach 1.
The inner diameter of the nozzle exhaust exit plane. Larger engines produce more thrust.
The maximum rate of propellant mass that passes through the nozzle.
The pressure inside the combustion chamber at full throttle. Higher pressure produces higher thrust and usually burns more efficiently.
The pressure of the gas exiting the nozzle.
The propellant(s) which this engine burns.
The ratio of the nozzle exit area to the nozzle throat area.
The ratio of the nozzle exit area to the nozzle throat area. Higher ratios produce higher specific impulse, but less thrust.

The temperature the thermal core heats the working fluid to. This is set by the heat source, not by the propellant.

Fields: Attitude error (deg) inside which the upright servo stays idle. Needed so a settled kitten can fall asleep instead of micro-correcting forever.
Bepu contact friction for the kitten's ground pairs while the traction servo is active. Kept low so the servo owns grip instead of fighting the contact solver.
Body tilt from gravity-up beyond which a grounded kitten counts as knocked over and drops into Tumbling.
Body tilt from gravity-up the kitten must be within before any mode may hand over to Grounded (hysteresis pair with Tip Over Tilt).
Buoyancy/weight ratio at or above which a contact-free kitten enters Swimming. Same rule for ocean and dense gas.
Buoyancy/weight ratio at or below which Swimming exits to Airborne. Keep below the enter ratio - the gap is the hysteresis.
Cap (m/s) on the velocity spent closing position error to the anchor. Governs how fast a fresh grab pulls in.
Cap (rad/s) on the angular rate spent closing orientation error to the anchor. High values can collapse the adaptive physics timestep.
Climb speed (m/s) the ladder clip was authored at; playback rate = Ladder Climb Speed / this.
Contact-free time (s) after which Tumbling hands over to Airborne.
Cross-fade time (s) when switching locomotion clips.
Damping rate (1/s) on vertical velocity while swimming; settles surface bobbing. 0 = free bob.
Degrees to pitch the eye look-at up in the ladder pose, compensating the clip's head-back tilt.
Distance (m) the physics body is held off the rail. Keep large enough that a releasing kitten is clear of the host's colliders.
Distance (m) the rendered kitten appears off the rail; the mesh is shifted in from the physics standoff to this. Match the climb clip's paw reach.
Duration (s) of the ease when handing off between ladder parts. Only applies across handoffs - normal climbing tracks the rail exactly. 0 = instant snap.

During the landing-assist window the upright servo may draw on the real landing impulse, capped at this multiple of its normal gravity-scaled clamp. Counters the momentum-scaled touchdown pitch kick that face-plants running jumps at low g.
Exponential time constant (s) for closing the gap to the target ground velocity. Lower = snappier acceleration and stops.
Friction when in Tumble state. Kept high enough that tumbles bleed off and settle.
Friction-style cap on traction: max grip acceleration = coeff x local gravity. Too low and the kitten slides on slopes.
Grace (s) after losing ground contact during which the kitten still counts as grounded.
Gravity (m/s^2) at or above which the moonwalk blend weight is zero.
Gravity (m/s^2) at or below which the ground gait is pure moonwalk.
Ground speed (m/s) below which the idle clip plays instead of walk/run.
Ground speed (m/s) the run clip was authored at; playback rate scales by actual speed / nominal.
Ground speed (m/s) the walk clip was authored at; playback rate scales by actual speed / nominal.

Half-life (s) for the attitude servo rotating the body onto the swim tilt - the swim-only replacement for Upright Half Life, so grounded righting is unaffected. Lower = snaps forward faster. If it stops responding, the rate clamp is binding: raise Swim Angular Budget Factor.
Half-life (s) of the facing (yaw) servo. Lower = turns into the movement direction faster.
Half-life (s) of the filtered ground normal the upright servo stands square to. Smooths pose over bumpy terrain.
Half-life (s) of the upright attitude servo. Lower = rights itself faster.
Half-life (s) smoothing the tilt target as speed and direction change.
Half-life (s) the treading/swim blend weight lerps toward its speed-derived target, so the pair fades instead of snapping. 0.01 = effectively instant.

How long (s) the kitten must stay airborne after touchdown before the landing recovery gives way to the flail again. Bounces shorter than this are ignored so the recovery plays once, continuously, instead of restarting.
How strongly grab selection prefers nodes in front of the kitten. 0 = pure nearest; higher = a node ahead beats a nearer one behind.
Input-free time (s) before a kitten on an on-rails host parks: body sleeps on rails, pose frozen relative to the host.
Input-free, settled time (s) before an idle swimmer parks: constrained physics drops to the cheap analytic ocean path. Any input un-parks instantly.
Lower clamp on the walk/run playback rate scaling.
Max distance (m) to a grab node for the [F] Grab prompt, and for handoffs past a rail's ends.
Max slew rate (rad/s) of the MMU auto-attitude toward the camera orientation in View mode.
Max swim thrust acceleration (m/s^2) toward the commanded direction.

Multiplies Tumble Traction Pair Friction as the kitten rolls nose-down, so a face-plant digs in instead of skating. Full value at muzzle-into-terrain, fading to 1x at nose-level and above. 1 = no boost.
Nominal speed (m/s) the run-gait nominal lerps toward as the moonwalk weight rises.
Nominal speed (m/s) the walk-gait nominal lerps toward as the moonwalk weight rises.

Nudges a seat occupant relative to its IVASeat, in seat axes: X forward (the way the kitten faces), Y right, Z up. Metres, and not scaled by the seated model scale, so it moves 1:1. The crew portrait face-cam tracks it.

Playback rate multiplier for the tumble/flail clip, in Tumbling and in the post-jump airborne flail. 1 = authored speed. Unlike the walk/run/ladder entries above this is a flat rate, not a speed the clip was authored at.
Playback-rate multiplier at full moonwalk weight; lerps from 1 as gravity falls. Below 1 = slower, floatier strides for the same ground speed.

Scales the achieved body tilt into the eye look-cone pitch offset while swimming, so the gaze keeps finding the camera instead of clamping to the whites. 1 = cancel the tilt exactly, 0 = off, negative flips the direction.
Scales the per-step angular rate budget of the attitude servos. 0 disables them entirely (no righting, no facing).
Scales the swim attitude servo's authority relative to the gravity-scaled grounded cap. 0 disables swim righting/tilt.
Seconds after entering Grounded that the landing assist stays available.

Seconds of the jump extro (landing recovery) clip to play before handing back to the idle/walk clip. The authored clip is 1.46s but stops moving at 0.42s, so the tail is a static hold. 0 = play the clip in full.
Speed (m/s) a tumbling kitten must stay under, in ground contact, for the settle timer to run.
Speed (m/s) the kitten moves along the rail while W/S is held.
Steepest slope (deg) the kitten stands square to. On steeper ground it leans only this far from gravity-plumb.
Swim speed (m/s) at which the body tilt reaches Swim Tilt High (deg).
Swim speed (m/s) at which the body tilt reaches Swim Tilt Low (deg).
Swim speed (m/s) at which the treading-water/swim anim blend is pure swim. 0 m/s is always pure treading.
Swim speed (m/s) the swim clip was authored at. The blended pair's playback rate = actual speed / nominal, clamped to never drop below 1x so the treading stride keeps its authored cadence.
Tangential speed (m/s) at which ground contact knocks the kitten into Tumbling instead of landing.
Target speed (m/s) the swim velocity servo drives toward while input is held.
Target swim speed (m/s) while Sprint (Shift) is held - the run analog.
Tilt from vertical (deg) at the high-speed knee; also the clamp above it.
Tilt from vertical (deg) at the low-speed knee.
Time (s) after a jump during which lingering ground contact is ignored, so liftoff isn't cancelled by the contact that launched it.
Time (s) the settle condition must hold before Tumbling hands over to Rightening.
Upper clamp on the walk/run playback rate scaling.
Upward velocity change (m/s) applied by a jump.
Yaw error (deg) inside which the facing servo stays idle.
(0 = treading, 1 = swim; the played weight lerps toward this)

accumulated contact impulse, up/facing error angle, current anim clip

Fields: m, so dents on coarse meshes will be shallower.
'Dropped' means a hit arrived with no slope budget left where it landed.

A dent at the current depth and radius settings, at a random point on a random dentable part's bounds, pushed toward its centre. Bypasses the contact path, so it lands on parts that have no collider too.
Ceiling repeated hits on one spot saturate toward, as a fraction of the scale radius. Above the single-hit depth, so only merging reaches it.
Dent depth, as a fraction of the scale radius, when a step's pressure equals the crash tolerance. Scales linearly below that.

Every dent on every vehicle in view, from the same vehicle-space dents the shader reads. Cyan ring = footprint radius on the surface, blue closes the sphere, orange spike = push direction with the dent's depth as its length. Stays on with this window closed, but hides with the rest of the UI.
Footprint radius is this many times the contact patch's equivalent radius, sqrt(area / pi), before clamping.
Fraction of the part's crash tolerance a contact step must reach to leave a dent. Below it, pad settling and gentle docking leave no mark.
Glancing contacts are rotated toward the surface's inward normal until their inward component reaches this. A sideways push shears the skin instead of denting it.
Graphics setting 'Impact Dents' is off: parts render undented

How big the triangles are: min(R, h)^2 / 2 of the coarsest triangle a dent lands on. The slope bound keeps the smooth field injective, but the mesh is flat triangles; this and 'min gap' bound how far a triangle's chord may stray from it. Either at 0 turns the guard off.
How thin the walls are: the smallest distance from a skin to whatever sits behind it. Either this or 'chord factor' at 0 turns the guard off.
Largest footprint, as a fraction of the scale radius. A footprint this size routinely reaches the neighbouring part.
Lipschitz bound on the displacement field. Below 1 the deformation is injective: nothing can pass through anything, however deep the dents.
Live multiplier on every stored dent's depth. Above the slope budget it is cancelled by the safety scale - widen dents to go deeper instead.
Master switch for gameplay dents. The graphics setting 'Impact Dents' must also be on for parts to render dented.
Off: slope budget only. Thin, coarsely-meshed walls may show chords crossing.
Removes every dent on the controlled vehicle.
Smallest footprint, as a fraction of the scale radius.
The fixed radius that 'part radius influence' lerps toward at 0. Unused at influence 1.

What the 'x radius' fractions above are fractions of. 1 = the part's own radius, so dents scale with whatever they land on. 0 = the fixed reference radius, so a given impact leaves the same size dent on a strut as on a tank. Between the two lerps.
